Subject: New SOW questions: billing buckets & anchor pricing

Sergio —

Thanks for the updated SOW (attached). Procurement reviewed the pricing annex and a couple of items need clarification before we route to legal:

1) Bucketization / anchor pricing: The SOW references "anchored bucket tiers" for committed volume. Can you explain, in plain terms, how a request is assigned to a bucket? Specifically: is bucketing based on per-call input+output tokens, or on aggregated daily/session totals? How does that interact with our long-chat flows (multi-turn conversation persisted across calls)?

2) Rounding & minimums: We see language about a billing quantum and minimum per request. Examples in your prior notes were helpful but we need a firm rule we can include in the contract. If a single streaming call generates 37 tokens, do you round up to the quantum? Are there exceptions for system prefix reuse/kv cache hits?

3) Discounts & tier anchoring: The 15% discount for Tier B looks attractive, but the SOW ties the anchor to "committed bucket coverage". Can you describe how overages and underutilization are credited/true-upped? Also confirm whether burst capacity is billed differently.

Attached: AvaRetail_SOW_v2.pdf (redline) and a CSV with our expected call distribution. Could someone on your team provide a short worked example (say: 3 sample calls with varying lengths) so Procurement can validate the math?

We'd like to have final pricing language by EOD Friday if possible — procurement is on a tight sprint.

Thanks,

Mark —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary up front, then a short worked example and a couple of policy notes.

High level answers:
- Bucket assignment: We bill per request (input + generated output tokens) and then map that per-request usage into the bucket quantum. We also maintain a conversation-level prefix/KV cache credit that reduces billable tokens when the runtime can reuse cached context. Buckets are not based on daily aggregates for the per-request quantum — aggregates only matter for meeting committed coverage and applying tiered discounts.

- Rounding & minimums: Default quantum is 100 tokens (billing increments). There is a per-request minimum of 75 tokens when streaming or short calls are used (this prevents micro-request amortization). If KV cache fully satisfies the prompt (rare), that call can be credited back as a "cache hit" and billed at a special reduced minimum — we show the rules in the attached pricing_anchor_note.pdf.

- Discounts & true-ups: Commitments are evaluated monthly. If committed units are underused, we apply a standard true-up credit at the end of quarter; overages above committed capacity are billed at the overage rate specified in the SOW (burst capacity gets billed at the burst multiplier). We can include a cap on burst multiplier for the first 90 days if you want a softer landing.

Worked example (attached also as a spreadsheet):
1) Call A: user prompt 40 tokens, model output 60 tokens => raw = 100 tokens => billed = 100 (single quantum)
2) Call B: user prompt 10 tokens, output 27 tokens => raw = 37 tokens => billed = 75 (per-request minimum)
3) Call C (long chat turn): prompt 120 tokens, output 320 tokens => raw = 440 tokens => billed = 500 (rounded up to next 100 quantum)

Notes:
- If across multiple calls KV cache saves 80 tokens of repeated context, that savings is applied before rounding on each request (i.e., we decrement the billable token count first).
- For committed coverage, we sum billed tokens (post-rounding) across the billing month; discounts apply at the monthly invoice level according to the SOW tiers.

I'll attach a clean worked spreadsheet and a short explainer PDF. If you'd like, we can do a 20-minute call with Karthik to run through your CSV this afternoon.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Hey Mark —

Quick technical clarifications and a sample line-item calculation so procurement can drop the numbers into the SOW. Sergio's summary is correct; below is the exact arithmetic we use server-side (we'll include these clauses in the pricing exhibit if you want).

Rounding order (server-side):
1) Compute raw_tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens
2) Subtract cache_savings (if any) => effective_tokens = max(raw_tokens - cache_savings, 1)
3) Apply per-request minimum: effective_tokens = max(effective_tokens, per_request_minimum)
4) Round up to nearest quantum: billed_tokens = ceil(effective_tokens / quantum) * quantum

Sample numeric run (using SOW default quantum=100, per_request_minimum=75):
- Call A: raw 100, cache 0 => effective 100 => billed 100
- Call B: raw 37, cache 0 => effective max(37,75)=75 => billed 100 (round up to 100) => note: we bill 100 not 75 because quantum rounding happens after minimum
- Call C: raw 440, cache 80 => effective 360 => billed 400

This is important: your invoice line items will show billed_tokens (post-rounding). For committed coverage we compare your committed units to billed_tokens aggregated monthly. True-up credit is computed as (committed_units - billed_tokens) * committed_rate (if positive). Overage is billed at overage_rate * billed_tokens over commitment.

Edge cases: short bursts from automated heartbeat calls (<=10 tokens raw) are aggregated server-side in 1-minute windows and then treated as a single request for the purposes of minimums to avoid microbilling.

I've attached a short walk-through on cache credit behavior (kv_cache_credit_walkthrough.pdf). Happy to adjust quantum/minimum numbers if AvaRetail needs different granularity for smaller transactions.

- Karthik
